newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London mixed, wary of Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London mixed, wary of Wall Street.

text.p: U.S. stocks in London were mixed in quiet trading on Friday as wary investors sat back to wait for the afternoon's U.S. economic data and to see if Wall Street continued its record-breaking run.

"We're looking for the Dow to open a fraction lower...We just can't see this going any further. But then again, so many people have said that and been wrong," one dealer said, reflecting European suspicion of the Dow's strength.
Overnight, the Dow gained 38.76 points to close at 6,313.00, hitting its seventh consecutive record as economic data pointed to a slowing domestic economy and subdued inflation.
U.S. retail sales rose at a slower-than-expected pace in October and consumer price rises were in line with forecasts.

On Friday, dealers said investors would be looking for more reassurance on the economic front from U.S. capacity utilisation and industrial production data at 1415 GMT, and business inventories statistics at 1500 GMT.
Dealers said business was quiet in London. Movers included Boeing, down $3/8 at $92 on reports that U.S. airline USAir does not want to take on eight aircraft it ordered.
Other losers included General Motors, which was down $1/4 at $55-3/8.
A dealer said investors were concerned at a larger-than-expected charge taken by GM for the fourth quarter.

Eli Lilly was weaker, dropping $1/4 to $74-3/4, on news it had received a subpoena in October from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission related to a probe of the relationships between drug companies and pharmacy benefits management companies.
